summary.intent: Run the GSD (Get Shit Done) roadmap workflow for cipher-box: gap-close Phase 68's rotation VERIFICATION findings (plan → execute → verify), then, per user follow-up, actually stand up the local stack and run the full web-e2e suite to prove Phase 68 end-to-end rather than relying on unit tests.
summary.outcome: Phase 68 gap closure (68-11, 68-12) was planned, executed, and verified clean (14/14 must-haves, SDK tests green). The full local web-e2e run then exposed that login→browse flow is broken by ~46 'not implemented — phase 63/65' stubs (read-chain + write-chain wiring never done for the web app), which predate Phase 68. User directed a full fix rather than deferral, so a new combined Phase 68.1 'Web Client Runtime Integration' was scoped (read+write wiring, ~1 week+ effort) and scaffolded (ROADMAP, REQUIREMENTS, RESEARCH, CONTEXT, VALIDATION committed), with planning in progress at transcript end.

rotateReadFromNode in packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/engine.ts previously returned void, discarding the root's rotated {readKey, generation, sequenceNumber}; its only production caller is client.ts performScopeExitRotation

workflow: GSD orchestrator protocol: when a subagent is running, avoid touching files it's editing; wait for its return, then spot-check (SUMMARY presence, commit count, 'Self-Check: PASSED') before proceeding to the next wave

For single-plan sequential waves that share a modified file (e.g. two plans both touching client.ts across dependent waves), prefer running executors sequentially on the main working tree rather than isolated worktrees — avoids merge risk and worktree/pnpm-install overhead with zero parallelism benefit
GSD's commit-helper has a known false-negative: it can report 'commit_failed' when the commit actually landed — verify via `git log`/`git status` rather than retrying the commit

Before reusing a running dev server (e.g. `nest --watch` on :3000) instead of restarting it, verify it's serving current code (e.g. curl a route added in a recent commit) rather than assuming freshness from process age

When Playwright/e2e wrapper scripts echo a fixed exit message, check the actual test summary in the log rather than trusting the shell wrapper's own exit code — the wrapper's `exit 0` can mask a failed test run

Reading a page's error-context.md snapshot at the moment of Playwright timeout is an effective way to pinpoint root cause (found an alert/error text directly on the stalled page) rather than only reading stack traces
Use `git blame` on a newly-discovered stub/throw to confirm whether it predates the current work before treating it as caused by the current phase

Spawning a dedicated inventory/scope-mapping subagent before sizing a large deferred-work phase (read-chain stubs, then write-chain stubs) surfaced a second stub family (write-chain) that would have been missed if only the first inventory was trusted

friction: User's initial phase completion report presented gap-closure verification (unit-test tier) as sufficient, but the actual web UI flow was fundamentally broken — the SDK-tier 'passed' verification gave false confidence about end-to-end correctness

Full web-e2e suite run took ~23 minutes and only then revealed the root cause was unrelated to Phase 68 (pre-existing phase-63/65 stubs), a significant time cost to discover scope was far larger than assumed

Local environment state was messy before the e2e run: stale API process on :3000 from an 18h-old build, an 'unhealthy'-flagged but actually-healthy mock-ipns docker container, and conflicting watch processes on the same port, requiring manual triage before tests could run meaningfully

Scope estimate grew twice during the session: first from 'run web-e2e' to '17 read-chain stubs need wiring (~1 week)', then to '46 total stubs (read+write), roughly 2-3 weeks' after the write-chain inventory came back
